title: The Quiet Winter
premise: Mara Dunmore returns to the snowbound village of Hollowmere to bury her twin sister Nell, only to find the body in the coffin is not her sister's face. When the church bell—melted down in 1911—begins ringing at midnight, Mara learns that Nell, desperate and grieving their mother's death, performed an old rite to 'call back what was lost,' inviting something into the family line. Trapped by a blizzard with the villagers who all seem to remember a version of Mara that never happened, she must uncover what was invited in before the frost finishes writing its pattern on every window. In the end, Mara realizes the entity wears the faces of the forgotten dead, and she can only banish it by willingly remembering—and speaking aloud—the truth of Nell's death, which she has spent her whole life refusing to know.
about_author: Orsen Zhou is the pen name of a former mortuary archivist who spent six years cataloguing unclaimed remains in rural parish records before turning to fiction. They write horror about small communities, inherited grief, and the things families agree not to say out loud.

chapters.title: The Wrong Face
chapters.summary: Mara arrives in Hollowmere through falling snow to identify her twin sister's body, but the face in the coffin belongs to a stranger. The undertaker insists it is Nell Dunmore. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: disorientation and dread as grief curdles into suspicion.

chapters.title: Doors Counted
chapters.summary: Mara moves into the family house, counting doors and checking locks as she did as a child. She finds Nell's journal hidden under floorboards, its last pages torn out. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: uneasy nostalgia; the house feels occupied even when empty.

chapters.title: The Bell That Wasn't
chapters.summary: At midnight the church bell rings, though parish records confirm it was melted down in 1911. Villagers gather in the square, faces blank, mouths moving in unison. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: first open supernatural rupture; the village itself seems complicit.

chapters.title: Everyone Knew My Sister
chapters.summary: Mara questions neighbors about Nell's final weeks; each describes tender memories Mara has no memory of, as if Nell lived a parallel life here. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: gaslit loneliness—was she ever really Nell's twin?

chapters.title: Frost Writing
chapters.summary: Frost patterns appear on every window overnight, forming the same branching figure. Mrs. Aldersey, the oldest villager, warns Mara not to trace them with her finger. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: creeping inevitability; the cold is communicating.

chapters.title: The Rite of Return
chapters.summary: In the parish archive Mara finds a handwritten rite from 1911 called 'the Calling Back,' used by families who lost children to the winter. The last recorded use ended with the bell being melted down. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: horrified understanding dawning.

chapters.title: What Nell Wanted Back
chapters.summary: Flashback chapters alternate: Nell alone after their mother's funeral, begging Mara by phone to come home, being refused. POV: Nell (flashback). Emotional beat: heartbreak—Nell's desperation was answered, just not by Mara.

chapters.title: The Village That Remembers
chapters.summary: Villagers begin greeting Mara with intimate familiarity, recounting childhoods she never had. Her own memories start shifting to match theirs. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: terror of losing selfhood; memory as contested territory.

chapters.title: Snowed In
chapters.summary: The blizzard seals the roads. Phone lines die. Mara and Mrs. Aldersey barricade the house as something knocks politely at every door, one by one, all night. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: siege tension; found-family bond forms between two survivors.

chapters.title: The Knocking Guest
chapters.summary: The knocker speaks in Nell's voice, reciting shared twin memories with perfect accuracy—including one Mara has told no one. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: violation and longing tangled together; it knows her better than anyone alive.

Mrs. Aldersey reveals her grandmother survived the original calling: the entity takes the shape of whoever the village most needs back, then replaces everyone, one remembered life at a time. POV: Mara with Aldersey's testimony. Emotional beat: stakes clarified—this is extinction by affection.

chapters.title: The Torn Pages
chapters.summary: Mara finds the torn journal pages sewn into her mother's burial shroud lining: Nell's confession that she performed the rite, and a plea for forgiveness. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: grief sharpening into resolve; the truth has a physical cost.

chapters.title: Midnight Service
chapters.summary: Drawn to the church, Mara witnesses the congregation at a service for a bell that doesn't exist, singing a hymn in reverse. The vicar turns to her and says, 'You're late, Nell.' POV: Mara. Emotional beat: full horror—the village has decided who she is.

chapters.title: Twin Light
chapters.summary: Mara realizes the entity cannot fully mimic Nell because Nell isn't dead—she's inside it, still fighting, leaving errors in the mimicry like fingerprints. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: hope rekindled; love leaves flaws the thing can't copy.

chapters.title: The Pattern Completes
chapters.summary: The frost on the windows resolves into a map of the village with one house left unmarked: Mara's. The entity is saving her for last. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: countdown pressure; sunrise is hours away.

chapters.title: Aldersey's Sacrifice
chapters.summary: Mrs. Aldersey walks into the snow offering her own remembered dead—a son lost in 1968—to buy Mara time. The bell rings once and stops. POV: Mara watching from the window. Emotional beat: devastating cost of kindness; found family proven real.

chapters.title: Into the White
chapters.summary: Mara crosses the frozen fields toward the churchyard where the bell was buried in molten form in 1911, following the frost pattern backward. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: grim pilgrimage; she chooses to face the truth rather than hide.

chapters.title: The Bell Beneath
chapters.summary: Beneath the yew tree, the melted bell lies half-formed in the earth, ringing without sound. Within it Mara sees every person the village ever failed to mourn. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: awe and pity—the monster is made of unmourned grief.

chapters.title: Nell's Truth
chapters.summary: Inside the bell's silence, Mara finally remembers what she has refused since childhood: Nell died saving Mara from the ice when they were nine, and Mara let herself forget. Speaking it aloud cracks the bell. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: climax—memory as both wound and weapon.

chapters.title: Sunrise
chapters.summary: As dawn breaks, the entity unravels, releasing the villagers' stolen memories. Nell appears one last time—not accusing, only grateful to be truly known—and fades with the frost. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: catharsis; grief integrated instead of avoided.

chapters.title: The Funeral, Corrected
chapters.summary: Mara buries the stranger's body with full honors and holds a second service for Nell, telling the village the true story. The congregation weeps for a girl they now genuinely remember. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: mourning done right; community rebuilt on honesty.

chapters.title: Lights On, Doors Open
chapters.summary: Spring comes. Mara stays in Hollowmere, keeping the lights on not from fear but welcome, and leaves the front door unlocked for the first time. On the sill, a single thread of frost blooms—and melts. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; healing without forgetting.
